newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary farmers' border protest causes little delay.
newsitem.headline: Hungary farmers' border protest causes little delay.

text.p: Efforts by a group of hardline Hungarian farmers to disrupt border crossings on Wednesday had little effect on traffic as fewer farmers than expected turned out in support of the protest, border police said.
"If there were bottlenecks at any of the border crossings we didn't notice them," National Border Guard spokesman Attila Krisan told Reuters.

The farmers' union METESZ had planned to slow down traffic on Hungary's roads by blocking one lane and to hinder the flow of vehicles at frontiers with six neighbouring countries by repeatedly crossing the border with their cars.

At two south Hungarian frontier posts with Serbia, Roszke and Tompa, some 300 farmers drove their cars at a snail's pace up to the border but did not cross and caused queues only slightly longer than usual.
"We are more concerned about East European guest workers returning home for the Easter vacation," Lieutenant-Colonel Lajos Varga, commander of the Tompa border police told Reuters.

Zoltan Timar, deputy spokesman of National Border Guard said the only other border crossing so far affected was Gyula, on the Romanian border, where 30 vehicles had appeared but had decided not to cross the border after consultations with border guards on both sides.
"We don't know what they plan," said Timar. "They will probably move around on the road leading to the frontier, staying on the Hungarian side of the border."

Late on Tuesday night, Parliament voted overwhelmingly to inprove taxation and social security payment obligations for agricultural producers but METESZ leaders had said in advance the measures did not go far enough and would not prevent their protest action.

METESZ is one of the smaller but more radical of Hungary's almost 30 farmers' unions which have so far failed to establish a common stance over land ownership, distribution of subsidies and farming taxation.
Other unions have witheld support for the protests in advance of a planned round table conference on the future of Hungary's agriculture.

METESZ leader Gyula Kosa said he considered the protest successful despite the low turnout and denied that farmers had been put off by government accusations at the weekend that the movement had become political.
"We would let anyone join our march but we won't let them take the lead," he said.
